entries.title: True, yet hard to believe
entries.literal_meaning: This is true, yet it is not believed.
entries.explanation: The line calls a statement true while registering a failure of belief. The headword’s second sense supplies that reading of the shortened ending. Our interpretation attends to the gap between asserting truth and finding something convincing; the line itself does not establish whether an unnamed statement is actually true.
entries.meaning_odia: କଥାଟିକୁ ସତ ବୋଲି କହି ମଧ୍ୟ ବିଶ୍ୱାସ ହେଉନଥିବା ଅବସ୍ଥାକୁ ଧାଡ଼ିଟି ଧରେ। ଶେଷର ସଂକ୍ଷିପ୍ତ ପ୍ରୟୋଗ ବୁଝିବାରେ ଶବ୍ଦର ଦ୍ୱିତୀୟ ଅର୍ଥ ସାହାଯ୍ୟ କରେ। ଆମ ପାଠ ସତ ବୋଲି କହିବା ଓ ବିଶ୍ୱାସ ହେବା ମଧ୍ୟର ଫରକକୁ ଦେଖେ। ଅଜଣା କଥାଟି ପ୍ରକୃତରେ ସତ କି ନୁହେଁ, ଏଥିରୁ ନିର୍ଣ୍ଣୟ ହୁଏନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our reading distinguishes a claim of truth from the experience of believing it.
entries.odia_summary: ଆମ ପାଠ ସତ୍ୟର ଦାବିକୁ ବିଶ୍ୱାସ ହେବାର ଅନୁଭବଠାରୁ ଅଲଗା କରେ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ଜଣେ ପାଠକ ଅପ୍ରତ୍ୟାଶିତ ହିସାବ ଦେଖି ପୁଣି ଗଣିଲେ। ସଂଖ୍ୟା କିପରି ଆସିଲା ବୁଝିବା ପରେ ସେ କଥାଟି ମାନିଲେ। / A reader checks an unexpected calculation and understands how its result was reached. This is an invented application, not evidence for the saying’s origin.
entries.cultural_context: The quotation remains unfilled: it omits the headword’s ମନକୁ. Belief sense2, not approval sense1, supplies the literal rendering; no speaker identity or particular disputed fact is established.

entries.title: The nearby voice
entries.literal_meaning: The one who sleeps nearby speaks into the ear—can their words be distrusted?
entries.explanation: The question gives a nearby voice an apparent advantage. The dictionary places it under backbiting, making access to the listener part of the image. Our reading separates that closeness from reliability: being heard privately does not establish that a report is true. No spouse, gender or actual accusation is identified.
entries.meaning_odia: ପ୍ରଶ୍ନଟି ପାଖରେ ଥିବା ସ୍ୱରକୁ ଏକ ସୁବିଧା ଦେଉଥିବା ପରି ଲାଗେ। ଅଭିଧାନରେ ଏହା ଚୁଗୁଲି କହିବା ଅର୍ଥ ତଳେ ଅଛି। ଆମ ପାଠ ନିକଟତାକୁ ବିଶ୍ୱସନୀୟତାଠାରୁ ଅଲଗା କରେ—ଏକାନ୍ତରେ ଶୁଣିଲେ ବୋଲି କଥାଟି ସତ ହୋଇଯାଏନାହିଁ। ବକ୍ତା ପତି ବା ପତ୍ନୀ, କେଉଁ ଲିଙ୍ଗର ବା କେଉଁ ଅଭିଯୋଗ କରୁଛନ୍ତି, ଉତ୍ସ ତାହା କହେନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our reading asks whether private access is being mistaken for trustworthy evidence.
entries.odia_summary: ଆମ ପାଠ ପଚାରେ, ଏକାନ୍ତରେ କହିବାର ସୁଯୋଗକୁ ପ୍ରମାଣ ଭାବି ନିଆଯାଉଛି କି।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ସଭା ପୂର୍ବରୁ ଜଣେ ସଦସ୍ୟ ଆଉଜଣଙ୍କ ବିଷୟରେ ଧୀର ସ୍ୱରରେ କିଛି କହିଲେ। ଶ୍ରୋତା ସମ୍ପୃକ୍ତ ବ୍ୟକ୍ତିଙ୍କ କଥା ମଧ୍ୟ ଶୁଣିବାକୁ କହିଲେ। / Before a meeting, a listener declines to judge another member from a private report alone. This scene is invented.
entries.cultural_context: The earlier Krishna Singh Mahabharata Adi quotation illustrates whispering sense1. It is separate from this Dhaga under sense2 and does not establish its author.

entries.title: The fish advertises its worth
entries.literal_meaning: The bhakuda fish said: I am king among fish; make broth from my head and see how enjoyable it is.
entries.explanation: The talking fish supports its royal claim with an offer of its own head for cooking. Our reading follows that odd self-advertisement: praise of its worth comes through what someone else might enjoy. This is a playful reading of the boast, not a supplied moral about sacrifice or a tested cooking recommendation.
entries.meaning_odia: କଥା କହୁଥିବା ମାଛ ନିଜକୁ ରାଜା କହି ନିଜ ମୁଣ୍ଡ ରାନ୍ଧିବା କଥା ଆଗକୁ ଆଣେ। ଆମ ପାଠ ସେହି ଅଦ୍ଭୁତ ଆତ୍ମପ୍ରଶଂସାକୁ ଦେଖେ—ଅନ୍ୟଜଣଙ୍କ ଭଲ ଲାଗିବା ଭିତରେ ନିଜ ମୂଲ୍ୟ ଦର୍ଶାଯାଉଛି। ଏହା କଥାଟିର ରସମୟ ପାଠ; ଆତ୍ମତ୍ୟାଗର ଉପଦେଶ ବା ପରୀକ୍ଷିତ ରୋଷେଇ ପରାମର୍ଶ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our reading notices a boast that offers the speaker itself as evidence of its value.
entries.odia_summary: ଆମ ପାଠରେ ଆତ୍ମପ୍ରଶଂସାର ପ୍ରମାଣ ଭାବେ ବକ୍ତା ନିଜକୁ ଆଗକୁ ଆଣୁଛି।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ପାଠଚକ୍ରରେ ଜଣେ ମାଛର ଗର୍ବିତ ସ୍ୱରରେ ଧାଡ଼ିଟି ପଢ଼ିଲେ। ଅନ୍ୟମାନେ ଦେଖିଲେ, ପ୍ରଶଂସାରେ ନିଜକୁ କେମିତି ଖାଦ୍ୟ ଭାବେ ଆଗକୁ ଆଣିଛି। / Readers perform the boast and discuss its peculiar offer. This reading-circle scene is invented, not a cooking demonstration.
